FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Handloom and Khadi Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. This standard was first published in 1966. This standard has been revised to overcome encountered by the khadi industry in implementation of the standard. Following are the important changes carried out while revising this standard: a) For checking the conformity of the bedsheets to the requirements laid down in this standard, a provision has been made for testing of the samples in prevailing atmospheric conditions. However, in case of dispute, the samples shall be tested after conditioning in the standard atmospheric conditions. b) The standard provides for agreement between permissible number of defects in the bedsheet. the buyer and the seller with respect to difficulties

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard TEXTILES - BEDSHEETS, COTTON KHADI, BLEACHED - SPECIFICATION ( First Revision )
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes constructional particulars and other requirements of bedsheets, cotton khadi, bleached. 1.2 This standard dots not appearance, feel, shade, etc. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed at Annex A are necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3 ATMOSPHERIC TESTING, CONHITIONS FOR specify the general neps and other spinning defects. The approximate count of warp and weft yam is given in Table 1. 4.2 Cloth The cloth used in the manufacture be woven in dosuti weave. 4.2.1 The selvedges w.ell wQven. of bedsheets shall

of the cloth shall be firm and

4.2,2 The transverse ends of the bedsheet shall be hemmed to a depth of not less than 13 mm with raw edges having a turn-in of 6 mm. The stitching shall be firm and regular. The hemming shall be uniform and flat and the edges shall be properly secured. 4.2.3 The bedsheets shall be free from dressing and filling materials and substances liable to cause subsequent tendering. 4.2.4 The bedsheets be reasonably free processing defects. 5 REQUIREMENTS when visually examined, from spinning, weaving shall and

Test specimens may be conditioned and tested in the prevailing atmospheric conditions for checking the conformity of the bedsheets to the standard. However, in case of dispute, the specimens shall be conditioned and tested in the standard atmosphere as specified in the referred Indian Standards on test methods. 4 GENERAL 4.1 Yarn The yarn used in the manufacture of bedsheets shall be hand-spun from clean carded cotton. It shall be reasonably even and free from leaf particles, slubs, Table 1 Constructional count of Tarn (for guidahce only) Universal Count (Cotton Count)

The quantity of the bedsheets delivered to buyer against one despatch note shall constitute a lot. 9.2 The conformity of the lot to the various requirements specified in the standard shall be determined on the basis of tests carried out on the samples selected from the lot. 9.3 Unless otherwise agreed, the number of pieces selected at random for inspection shall be in accordance with Table 3. Sample Size

Lenght and width of the bedsheets when determined in accordance with IS 1954 : 1990 shall be as agreed to between the buyer and the seller or as declared by the seller. However, a tolerance of +3 cm shall be permitted on length and width. 5.4 Sealed Samples

5.4.1 If in order to illustrate or specify the indeterminable characteristics, such as general appearance, lustre, feel, etc, a sample has been agreed upon and sealed, the supply shall be in conformity with the sample in such respects. 5.4.2 The custody of the sealed sample shall be a matter of prior agreement between the buyer and the seller. 6 INSPECTION 6.1 The bedsheets when visually inspected shall be free from the major flaws given in Annex B. However, permissible number of major flaws per piece may be as agreed to between the buyer and the seller. 6.2 For details of the flaws mentioned in 6.1, a reference may be made to IS 4125 : 1987. 7 MARKING 7.1 The bedsheet shall be legibly following information : a) b) c) marked with the
